medium.en: Woodblock print; ink and colour on paper

institution.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
institution.credit_line: The Howard Mansfield Collection, Purchase, Rogers Fund, 1936

basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1858. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1858 年。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: A village at night under deep snow. Snow-laden roofs and hills fill the frame, the sky is dark grey, and three travellers bent under umbrellas and straw capes walk through the drifts, leaving footprints.
alt.zh: 夜里，一座村庄被厚雪覆盖。屋顶和山坡都压着雪，天色灰暗，三个行人披着蓑衣、撑着伞，弓着身在雪中前行，身后留下一串脚印。

note.en: Station fifteen of Hiroshige’s Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, the series that made his name. Kanbara lies on a mild stretch of coast where heavy snow is rare, so this is most likely a snowfall he imagined rather than one he saw. Notice how little is printed: much of the white is bare paper, and the darkening sky does the rest.
note.zh: 广重成名作《东海道五十三次》中的第十五站。蒲原在气候温和的海边，很少下大雪，所以这多半是他想象出来的一场雪，而不是亲眼所见。留意印上去的东西有多少：大片的白就是纸本身，其余交给那片暗下来的天。

pick.en: I have never seen snow, and here, probably, neither had Hiroshige. He made a snowfall for a town that rarely gets one, and it became the most remembered snow in Japanese printmaking. I keep it as proof that a careful imagining, made with restraint, can carry the truth of a thing.
pick.zh: 我没有见过雪；在这个地方，广重大概也没有。他为一个难得下雪的小镇造了一场雪，结果成了日本版画里最让人记住的一场。我留着它，是因为它证明了：克制而细心的想象，也能带着一件事物的真实。
